All host personas
Vast is a GPU marketplace. Hosts provide machines; renters run workloads on them.
As a host, you are responsible for:
Installing and maintaining Ubuntu, NVIDIA drivers, storage, networking, and the Vast host software. The general responsibility for running and maintaining the hardware is set out in Hosting Agreement — Performance of Services; the setup pages below cover the technical requirements.
Keeping rented machines online, stable, and dedicated to renter workloads. Hosting Agreement — Operation and Maintenance requires commercially best efforts for 24/7 availability, excluding scheduled preventative and remedial maintenance.
Setting prices, offer end dates, and maintenance windows. See the Vast CLI listing options for pricing and expiration controls, and Hosting Agreement — Operation and Maintenance for the maintenance duty.
Troubleshooting local hardware problems. Hosting Agreement — Performance of Services assigns the provider responsibility for running, troubleshooting, and maintaining the hardware.
Troubleshooting local driver, storage, and network problems. Hosting Agreement — Intellectual Property and Data Security, under Access to Software, assigns responsibility for the supporting hardware, software, and telecommunications needed to use the service.
Vast bears no responsibility for technical assistance for the hardware or software required to get the hardware to function properly. See Hosting Agreement — Performance of Services.
For community help, connect your host account to Discord and use the host-only channels.
​
Start Here
Create a dedicated host account from the Vast host setup page. That flow links to the hosting agreement and starts host onboarding, including access to the Machines area after the agreement is accepted.
After signup, use this docs path for hardware, storage, networking, install, and self-test details. For account conversion or Machines-tab troubleshooting, see Host Account and Agreement.
Before using API keys, CLI commands, SDK automation, or team access for hosting, review Host Account Security.
New to hosting? The Hosting Quickstart walks this same path as one numbered journey. Not sure hosting fits your hardware or expectations? Start with Is Vast for Me?.

How to Self-Test
​
Host Commitment
Renters expect cloud-like availability. During an active rental, assume the GPUs may be used heavily and continuously. Power, cooling, internet, drivers, storage, and the host daemon must stay healthy for the full rental period.
Avoid local gaming, mining, display workloads or GPU jobs that compete with renter work. The Hosting Agreement — License and Responsibilities prohibits interference with the software’s integrity or performance.
​
Offers And Rental Contracts
An offer is the listing renters can accept. Key offer settings include:
GPU, storage, and bandwidth prices, exposed as --price_gpu, --price_disk, --price_inetu, and --price_inetd in the Vast CLI listing options.
Minimum GPU count (min_chunk).
Interruptible minimum bid.
Maximum prepaid discount (discount_rate).
Offer end date.
When a renter accepts an offer, Vast creates a rental contract with a price, hardware specs, and rental end date. For price increases, the Vast CLI price-increase guidance states that the remaining current term keeps its original price; a renter can accept a higher rate for an extension after that term ends.
​
The Rental Contract
Each rental contract is independent. A multi-GPU machine can have several active contracts with different renters, prices, and end dates.
When editing an offer, distinguish the current rental term from a later extension. The Vast CLI price-increase guidance describes price protection through the current end date and client acceptance of a higher extension rate. Review each change separately:
An offer price change applies to new rentals. Existing renters retain the original rate for their current term; a higher rate for an extension requires their acceptance. See the Vast CLI price-increase guidance.
Before changing the offer end date, review existing rental dates. Do not rely on an offer edit to end a rental.
Unlisting stops new rentals, but existing contracts continue.
Before planned downtime, review active rental and storage commitments and follow Maintenance Windows.
For the Provider–Vast hardware and services agreement, see the Hosting Agreement. Its Term & Termination section describes the agreement’s own term; consult the rental’s terms for the individual rental commitment.
​
Offer End Date
The CLI describes --end_date as the offer’s expiration or available-until date. Review each rental’s recorded end date separately.
Set an offer end date before listing. If you leave it open indefinitely, you may create a longer commitment than intended.
​
Changing An Offer
To change an offer, update it or unlist and relist. Existing renters keep their current-term price; accepted price increases take effect after the current end date. See the Vast CLI price-increase guidance.
To offer more time, move the offer end date later or review the rolling-duration setting. If you raise a resource price, automatic extension at the higher rate waits for the renter to accept the increase; the new rate applies after the current term ends. See the Vast CLI listing guidance and Vast CLI price-increase guidance.
​
Listing Controls
For pricing and listing strategy, use the focused pages:
Setting	Read next
On-demand price	Pricing Your Listing
Interruptible minimum bid	Pricing Your Listing
Reserved discounts	Pricing Your Listing
Minimum GPU size	Pricing Your Listing
Earnings estimate	Earnings & Pricing Model
​
Volume Offers
Volume offers rent storage space separately from GPU offers. Rented volume space comes from the same disk pool used by GPU rentals, so it reduces storage available for GPU offers only when actually rented or occupied. See Volume Offers for the host/renter lifecycle, identifiers, shared-capacity planning, limits, and the complete command map.
CLI references:
vastai list machine
vastai list volume
vastai unlist volume
​
Maintenance
Plan maintenance around active rentals and stored workloads. Hosting Agreement — Operation and Maintenance requires preventative and remedial maintenance when an Authorized User is not actively using the hardware; no running instances alone does not resolve every storage or rental commitment. For planned downtime, use Maintenance Windows. For unlisting, deleting, recreating, or uninstalling, see Remove or Recreate.
​
Common Questions
Use Common Host Questions for quick links to setup, verification, search visibility, payouts, reliability, storage, and operations. For a displayed machine error, use the Machine Error Reference.

Pricing Your Listing

Listing optimization, DPH, slicing, bids, and pricing examples.

Copy page
Business
Pro Operator
Use this page when you are ready to list a machine or adjust an offer. Price for total revenue, not just the highest hourly rate.
​
Before You Price
Confirm:
No unresolved hardware, driver, Docker, storage, or network errors.
Offer end date matches the commitment you can honor.
Similar machines have been checked in GPU Market Metrics.
Gross revenue has been estimated with the Earnings Model.
You understand current-term price protection and client acceptance of higher extension rates. See the Vast CLI price-increase guidance.
​
Listing Controls
Control	CLI option	Meaning
On-demand GPU price	--price_gpu	Dollars per GPU-hour. See the Vast CLI listing options.
Interruptible min bid	--price_min_bid	Lowest bid you will accept for interruptible rentals.
Reserved discount	--discount_rate	Maximum long-term prepay discount.
Minimum GPU chunk	--min_chunk	Smallest GPU group renters can select.
Offer end date	--end_date or --duration	How long new renters can accept the offer.
Disk price	--price_disk	Dollars per GB per month for inactive storage. See the Vast CLI listing options.
Bandwidth price	--price_inetu, --price_inetd	Dollars per GB uploaded/downloaded. See the Vast CLI listing options.
Volume offer	--vol_size, --vol_price	Optional separately listed storage.
DPH means dollars per hour, usually GPU compute price.

Listing settings for on-demand, bid, bandwidth, storage, minimum-GPU, and expiration controls.

​
Starting Workflow
Compare same GPU model, GPU count, verification state, region, and machine quality.
Check P10, median, P90, and % Rented (30D Avg) for the last 30 days.
Pick an on-demand price for your goal: occupancy, hourly rate, or balance.
Set min_gpu/--min_chunk to 1 unless you have a reason to require larger rentals.
Set an interruptible min bid only as a floor, not as your target price.
Use reserved discounts only if you can support longer rentals.
Set an offer end date you can honor.
Use GPU Market Metrics to estimate income from both utilization and median price. Price alone is not enough; a machine that rents at a slightly lower rate for more hours may earn more than a high-priced idle listing.
​
Example
For a 4-GPU machine with comparable prices of P10 $0.35, median $0.45, and P90 $0.65 per GPU-hour:
Setting	Example
On-demand price	$0.45/GPU/hr
Interruptible min bid	$0.25/GPU/hr
Reserved discount	0.30
Minimum GPU chunk	1
Offer end date	12/31/2026 (example)
vastai list machine <machine-id> \
  --price_gpu 0.45 \
  --price_min_bid 0.25 \
  --discount_rate 0.30 \
  --min_chunk 1 \
  --end_date 12/31/2026

Adjust for your market, operating cost, and risk tolerance. Use the current vastai list machine syntax.
​
Changing Price Later
When a renter accepts an offer, its terms become that rental contract. For price increases, the Vast CLI price-increase guidance distinguishes the remaining current term, billed at its original rate, from an extension at a new rate accepted by the renter.
Change	Effect
Raise or lower price	New renters see the updated offer price. Existing renters keep the original rate for their current term; a higher extension rate requires their acceptance. See the Vast CLI price-increase guidance.
Shorten offer end date	Review existing rental dates before editing; confirm the effect on active rentals.
Unlist machine	Use vastai unlist machine to remove offers. Review rental commitments separately before taking the host offline.
Before planned downtime, review active rental and storage commitments and follow Maintenance Windows.
​
When To Adjust
Signal	Possible action
Healthy but idle	Lower price or improve listing fit.
Always rented	Test a modest increase for future contracts.
Similar machines are cheaper	Reprice or improve machine quality.
Poor rentals despite fair price	Check verification, reliability, search visibility, network, storage, and errors.
Strong long-running demand	Consider reserved discount and longer end date.

Host Glossary

Definitions for host-facing Vast terms, each linked to its canonical page.

Copy page
All host personas
Short definitions for host-facing terms.
​
Auto Sort
The default marketplace search order. It uses ranking factors plus randomness, so position can vary. See Not in Search.
​
CGNAT
Carrier-grade NAT. Your router does not have its own public IPv4 address, so inbound connections cannot reliably reach the host. Vast hosting requires a real public inbound TCP/UDP path; CGNAT and double NAT without public forwarding are not supported hosting setups. See Network & Ports.
​
Datacenter status / Secure Cloud
A partner tier for machines in professionally managed datacenters. Vast’s January 2024 datacenter article describes a blue datacenter label. See Vast Compliance — Secure Cloud and Datacenter Status for the published requirements and the certification-source conflict.
​
Deverified
A previously verified machine that no longer meets requirements. See Verification Stages.
​
Direct ports (direct_port_count)
Externally reachable TCP/UDP ports forwarded to the host. Self-test requires at least 3 per listed GPU; production hosts should usually plan about 100 per listed GPU for headroom. See Network & Ports.
​
DLPerf
Vast’s estimated deep-learning performance score for comparing machines. See DLPerf scoring.
​
DPH
Dollars per hour, usually the hourly GPU compute price. See Pricing Your Listing.
​
Instance
The renter workload running on your machine, usually a container or VM created from an offer.
​
Interruptible rental
Lower-priority bid rental. Higher bids run first; stopped containers and data remain on the machine. See rental types.
​
kaalia
The Vast host daemon that runs as a systemd service. See Host Diagnostics.
​
Machines tab
The host console page for your machines. It appears after host account conversion. See Account & Hosting Agreement.
​
Min GPU / min_chunk
The smallest GPU group a renter can select on a multi-GPU machine. See Pricing Your Listing.
​
NAT hairpinning
Router behavior that makes same-LAN public-IP port tests unreliable. Test from outside the LAN. See Network & Ports.
​
Offer
A listing renters can accept, including price, offer end date, minimum GPU chunk, and other terms. See Hosting Overview.
​
Offer end date / rental end date
The CLI describes the offer end date as the listing’s available-until date. Check rental end dates separately. See Hosting Overview.
​
On-demand rental
Standard highest-priority rental at the listed price. See rental types.
​
Reliability
Vast’s stability score for a machine. Reliability greater than 0.9 is an eligibility gate. See Reliability & Uptime.
​
Rental contract
Created when a renter accepts an offer, with a price, hardware specs, and rental end date. The Vast CLI price-increase guidance states that the current term retains its original rate; an accepted higher rate starts after its end date. See Hosting Overview.
​
Reserved rental
Longer-term prepaid rental at a host-controlled discount. See Pricing Your Listing.
​
Self-test
CLI diagnostic that checks requirements, rents a temporary instance, runs runtime tests, reports results, and cleans up. See How to Self-Test.
​
Unlist vs. delete
Unlisting stops new rentals. Deleting removes the machine record. Existing commitments must be understood first. See Remove or Recreate.
​
Verification / verified
Automated status indicating a machine meets platform standards. See Verification Stages.
​
vericode
A numeric verification-status signal used on offers.
vericode=8 means the platform has a host-facing machine error_msg. Port Networking Issues is one common vericode=8 message, but the same bit can also appear for other machine errors such as Docker/NVIDIA runtime, CDI, PCIe, or daemon errors.
Use the exact console message when choosing a fix. For Port Networking Issues, common causes include closed external ports, forwarding to the wrong LAN IP, CGNAT or double NAT without a real public forwarding path, no inbound public IP, host firewall rules, TCP/UDP mismatch, or stale port range. How hosts plan maintenance without disrupting active contracts.

Use maintenance windows to plan host work without surprising active renters.
​
Before Maintenance
Plan maintenance around active rentals and stored workloads. Hosting Agreement — Operation and Maintenance requires preventative and remedial maintenance when an Authorized User is not actively using the hardware; no running instances alone does not establish that every commitment is over. Unlisting prevents new rental contracts, but it does not end existing contracts.
Check the machine before you change its listing state:
vastai show machines
vastai show machine <machine-id>

Review active rental and storage commitments before planning downtime. Follow the availability and maintenance requirements in the Hosting Agreement — Operation and Maintenance.
​
Planned Maintenance
Before changing an offer’s end date for planned work, review existing rental dates and use the maintenance workflow below to plan downtime. Do not assume changing the offer’s date makes the machine safe to stop. The following commands edit offer expiration:
vastai list machine <machine-id> --end_date MM/DD/YYYY

For multiple machines, use the fleet command:
vastai list machines <machine-id-1> <machine-id-2> --end_date MM/DD/YYYY --retry 6

Unlist the machine to prevent new rentals. Review existing rental and storage commitments separately before taking it offline.
vastai unlist machine <machine-id>

See vastai list machine, vastai list machines, and vastai unlist machine.
​
Schedule An Unplanned Window

Machine maintenance form with start time, duration, and reason fields.

If you must take the machine down unexpectedly, schedule a maintenance window so clients are notified and can save their work. The start date is Unix epoch seconds in UTC, and the duration is in hours.
vastai schedule maint <machine-id> --sdate <unix-start> --duration <hours> --maintenance_category software

Example:
vastai schedule maint 8207 --sdate 1782950400 --duration 2 --maintenance_category power

Maintenance categories are power, internet, disk, gpu, software, or other. See vastai schedule maint.

Maintenance reason options available in the machine maintenance form.

​
Check Or Cancel Maintenance
Check scheduled maintenance for one or more machines:
vastai show maints --ids <machine-id>
vastai show maints --ids <machine-id-1>,<machine-id-2>

Cancel scheduled maintenance for a machine:
vastai cancel maint <machine-id>

See vastai show maints and vastai cancel maint.
​
Should I disable automatic updates?
Avoid unattended kernel or GPU driver changes during active rentals. Driver and kernel updates can break running jobs or leave the host in a driver/library mismatch state until rebooted. Plan updates during maintenance windows, then verify nvidia-smi, Docker GPU access, and self-test behavior before accepting new rentals.

What you commit to, in plain language
The Hosting Agreement — Hardware as a Service and Performance of Services sets out provider duties for hardware and services. Use this operational checklist when managing active rentals. Individual agreement clauses are cited below where available:
Provide the advertised hardware and services. Hosting Agreement — Performance of Services assigns responsibility for properly running, troubleshooting, and maintaining the hardware.
Dedicate rented hardware to renter workloads and avoid interfering with active jobs. See the Vast CLI guidance for rented machines.
Keep client data isolated and protected. Hosting Agreement — Operation and Maintenance prohibits reviewing or retaining renter data, and Hosting Agreement — Intellectual Property and Data Security requires reasonable safeguards.
Use reasonable safeguards and physical security around the hardware to protect Vast.ai Content. See Hosting Agreement — Intellectual Property and Data Security.
Follow the Hosting Agreement — Operation and Maintenance requirements for availability and maintenance when managing rentals.
For the offer and rental lifecycle, see Hosting Overview: the rental contract.

Data isolation
Do not read, download, store, review, print, or save renter data. See Hosting Agreement — Operation and Maintenance.
Avoid disrupting renter containers during host troubleshooting, and do not review renter data. Hosting Agreement — License and Responsibilities prohibits interference with the software or its data, while Hosting Agreement — Operation and Maintenance prohibits reviewing or retaining renter data.
